subject: Information Theory
title: The Immune System's Memory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Immune System's Memory.

hook.text: Your body remembers every infection it has fought. Memory T-cells store that information for decades. Biology has RAM.

buildup.text: After fighting a pathogen, memory cells remain. They encode what the threat looked like for rapid future response.

discovery.text: The immune system stores information about millions of potential threats using combinatorial receptor diversity.

twist.text: Vaccines exploit this: they provide information about a threat without the danger, pre-loading the immune memory.

climax.text: The immune system is an information system: detect, classify, remember, and respond. It learns from experience.

punchline.text: Your immune system remembers. Every infection leaves a lesson.

quiz.question: How do vaccines leverage the immune system's information storage?
options: They pre-load threat information without causing disease
